question_text: Find the coordinates of the vertex 'C' of △ABC if its centroid is the origin and the vertices A, B are (1,1,1) and (−2,4,1) respectively.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the centroid is in terms of the vertices, and how many equations that gives you.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the centroid formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. The centroid is the plain average of the vertices, one coordinate at a time. Write the formula with the unknown vertex in it and set it equal to the given centroid.
steps.memory_tip: A triangle's centroid is the plain average of three vertices — divide by 3.

recall.must_convey: That the centroid formula is written with the unknown vertex included and set equal to the given centroid.
accept: the centroid is the average of the vertices so write that and set it equal
add the coordinates and divide, then equate to the given centroid
write the centroid formula with the unknown vertex in it
centroid formula rasi given centroid ki equate cheyyali
set the average equal to the given point

steps.why: A centroid condition gives one equation per coordinate, and the three are completely independent — so each unknown coordinate falls out on its own.
common_mistakes: Dividing by the wrong number of vertices.
Mixing the x, y and z equations together.

steps.label: Solve for the third vertex
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Solve the three equations one at a time. Nothing links them, so this is three short subtractions rather than a system.
steps.memory_tip: Three independent equations, each one subtraction. The centroid at the origin makes every right side 0.

recall.must_convey: That solving each coordinate equation gives (1, −5, −2).
accept: solve each coordinate separately to get the vertex
the three equations are independent so do them one at a time
moodu coordinates separate ga solve cheyyali

steps.why: Each coordinate of a centroid depends only on the matching coordinates of the vertices, which is what makes the three equations separate.
common_mistakes: Carrying a value from the x equation into the y equation.
Sign slip on a negative coordinate.

insider_note: The centroid is the origin, so each coordinate sum is simply zero — the shortest form these equations ever take. Two of the three answers come out negative, and that is where the sign slips happen.
